title: Automate Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: A 2026 Guide
summary: Automate Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP by selecting REST APIs for single records or FBDI for bulk loads, with both methods included in your subscription.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Can you automate Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP without coding?


Yes for batch work, because file-based data import and the built-in scheduler run from the Fusion screens with no code, while REST calls need at least a short script. You fill in the import template, upload it, and schedule the load and import jobs.


That covers most recurring loads. Code only becomes necessary when another system has to push or pull data on its own trigger.


### Does Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP have RPA or an AI agent option?


Inside Fusion applications, Oracle ships some embedded AI features, and robotic process automation exists in the wider Oracle stack. Availability depends on your release and subscription, so confirm both before planning around them.


Screen-driving RPA is a fallback for the rare task that has neither a REST resource nor an import path. Where an API exists, calling it is more stable than clicking through a page that changes with each update.


### Is the REST API included in the Fusion licence?


In the usual subscription, the REST APIs come with the Fusion application itself, and we know of no separate per-call charge. Confirm that in your order document, because contracts differ.


The metered units to watch sit elsewhere. Oracle Integration is billed by messages processed, a unit you never incur when your own script calls REST directly.


Fusion can also throttle heavy request volumes, so design bulk work as file imports rather than thousands of single calls.


### How often does Oracle change the Fusion APIs?


On a regular release cadence, Oracle updates Fusion, and each update can add resources and fields. Deprecations are announced in the release notes ahead of removal.


Because resource paths carry a version, pin the version in your calls and read the release notes before each update reaches your environment. Run your scripts against a non-production instance first, so a changed field breaks a test run and not a close.


### What should you do on Monday?


Create a dedicated integration user in a non-production environment and give it a role that can read one business object, such as invoices or suppliers. Then make a single GET request against that REST collection with basic authentication and ask for the data only.


If it returns records, you have confirmed the credentials, the role, and the network path. Every later automation step relies on those three.
